species_class: Fallow Deer, Mule Deer, Sika Deer, White-tailed Deer, and Elk/Cervidae

indication.text: Sedation accompanied by a shorter period of analgesia in Cervidae (fallow, mule, sika and white-tailed deer and elk): to calm and facilitate handling of fractious animals, diagnostic procedures, minor surgical procedures, therapeutic sedation and pain relief after injury or surgery, and as a preanesthetic to local anesthetic
indication.quote: Xylazine should be used in Cervidae (Fallow Deer, Mule Deer, Sika Deer, White-tailed Deer and Elk) when it is desirable to produce a state of sedation accompanied by a shorter period of analgesia.

dose_regimen.dose: Fallow deer 2.0 to 4.0 mg/lb (4.4 to 8.8 mg/kg); mule, sika and white-tailed deer 1.0 to 2.0 mg/lb (2.2 to 4.4 mg/kg); elk 0.25 to 0.5 mg/lb (0.55-1.1 mg/kg)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Injectable 300 mg/mL sterile solution; may be used in conjunction with local anesthetics such as procaine or lidocaine
dose_regimen.quote: Fallow Deer (Dama dama) - 0.67 to 1.33 mL/100 lbs body weight (2.0 to 4.0 mg/lb or 4.4 to 8.8 mg/kg); M ule (Odocoileus hemionus), Sika (Cervus nippon) & White-tailed (Odocoileus virginianus) Deer - 0.33 to 0.67 mL/100 lbs body weight (1.0 to 2.0 mg/lb or 2.2 to 4.4 mg/kg); Elk (Cervus canadensis) - 0.08 to 0.17 mL/100 lbs Bodyweight (0.25 to 0.5 mg/lb or 0.55-1.1 mg/kg)

effectiveness.design: No new study. Supplemental approval (Category II change) adding a 300 mg/mL concentration; effectiveness rests on the formulation being identical to the approved AnaSed 100 mg/mL solution (same active and inactive ingredients, same pH)
effectiveness.result: No additional effectiveness studies were required for approval of the 300 mg/mL product
effectiveness.quote: Based on the formulation characteristics of the proposed xylazine product, no additional effectiveness studies were required for approval of the xylazine 300 mg/mL product.

notes: NOT a dog summary: species are fallow, mule, sika and white-tailed deer and elk (Cervidae). Supplemental NADA (Category II change) providing a 300 mg/mL xylazine concentration in addition to the approved 100 mg/mL; the summary is catalogued under Anased® but the document names the product Cervizine 300 Injectable (sponsor at approval: Lloyd, Inc.). No effectiveness, target animal safety, PK or adverse-reaction studies are reported; the summary states that no additional studies were required because the 300 mg/mL and 100 mg/mL solutions contain the same active and inactive ingredients buffered to the same pH. target_animal_safety left null for that reason. Dosing frequency is not stated. The dose quote preserves a PDF-extraction typo ('M ule').

indication.text: Sedation accompanied by a shorter period of analgesia in dogs and cats: diagnostic procedures, orthopedic procedures, dental procedures, minor surgical procedures of short duration, restraint of fractious animals, therapeutic sedation and pain relief after injury or surgery, and major surgical procedures as a preanesthetic to general anesthesia or with local anesthetics
indication.quote: Chanazine (xylazine) should be used in dogs and cats when it is desirable to produce a state of sedation accompanied by a shorter period of analgesia.

dose_regimen.dose: 0.5 mg/lb intravenously; 1 mg/lb intramuscularly or subcutaneously (0.5 mg/lb IM may suffice in dogs over 50 lbs)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Sedation usually maintained for 1 to 2 hours; analgesia lasts 15 to 30 minutes
dose_regimen.quote: Intravenously-0.5 mL/20 lbs body weight (0.5 mg/lb) Intramuscularly or subcutaneously-1 mL/20 lbs body weight (1 mg/lb) In large dogs (over 50 lbs), a dosage of 0.5 mg/lb administered intramuscularly may provide sufficient sedation and/or analgesia for most procedures.

effectiveness.design: Generic (ANADA) approval: no in vivo study. Safety and effectiveness established by chemical equivalence to the pioneer product Rompun® 20 mg/mL Injectable (NADA 047-955); waiver from in vivo bioequivalence testing granted under the Fifth GADPTRA Policy Letter
effectiveness.result: Waiver from an in vivo bioequivalence study was granted June 15, 1992 because the generic and pioneer products are solutions with the same active and inactive ingredients in the same concentrations and the same pH
effectiveness.quote: Based on the formulation characteristics of the generic product, Chanelle Manufacturing Pharmaceutical, Ltd. was granted a waiver June 15, 1992 (photocopy attached) from conducting an in vivo bioequivalence study with Chanazine® 20 mg/mL Injectable.

notes: Generic (ANADA 200-184) approval; the summary contains no new safety, effectiveness, PK or adverse-reaction studies. The 'effectiveness' entry records only the bioequivalence waiver / chemical-equivalence basis for approval. Species/Class is 'Dogs and cats'. Dosing frequency is not stated; the dose quote is from General Information (dosage given as mL of the 20 mg/mL solution per 20 lbs body weight).

indication.text: Xylazine reversing agent and antidote for use in dogs only
indication.quote: Xylazine Reversing Agent and Antidote For Use in Dogs Only

dose_regimen.dose: 0.05 mg/lb (0.11 mg/kg), given as 0.5 mL per 20 pound body weight
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Dose is that used in the pivotal field study (General Information lists no recommended dosage); in the field study yohimbine was injected 15 minutes after IV xylazine and 25 minutes after IM or SC xylazine
dose_regimen.quote: Dose in study was 0.5 mL yohimbine per 20 pound body weight (0.05 mg/lb or 0.11 mg/kg).

target_animal_safety.duration: 3 IV doses at 6 hr intervals (0, 6 and 12 hr); each dog observed for > or = 28 days with intensive testing for 24 hr after treatment
target_animal_safety.n_animals: 12 female and 12 male young healthy adult mixed-breed dogs in 4 groups

findings.finding: Dose groups: 0X diluent control (volume of 5X dose), 1X 0.05 mg/lb, 3X 0.15 mg/lb and 5X 0.25 mg/lb yohimbine, each given IV 3 times at 6 hr intervals
findings.quote: Each dog was administered the prescribed dose I.V. in a cephalic or saphenous vein 3 times at 6 hr intervals (0 time, 6 hr, and 12 hr).

findings.finding: No significant differences between control and treated groups in hematology, serum chemistry or urinalysis (Dunnett test)
findings.quote: there were no significant differences in hematology, serum chemistry, and urinalysis.

findings.finding: Necropsy and histopathology detected no treatment-related changes
findings.quote: A routine necropsy and a histopathology failed to detect any treatment related changes.

findings.finding: Yobine judged safe when dosed IV at 0.05, 0.15 and 0.25 mg/lb three times at 6 hour intervals
findings.quote: dosed I.V. at 0.05, 0.15 and 0.25 mg/lb body weight 3 times at 6 hour intervals.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: The study was designed to test the safety of yohimbine in dogs treated at 0, 1x, 3x, and 5x the intended dose. c. Test Animals: 12 female and 12 male young healthy adult dogs of mixed breed, which were randomly assigned to 4 test groups.

effectiveness.design: Multi-site placebo-controlled clinical field study (sites started after October 10, 1986; terminated June 1, 1987). Client-owned dogs of random age, sex, weight and breed sedated with xylazine (IV 0.5 mg/lb, IM 1.0 or 0.5 mg/lb, or SC 1.0 mg/lb, route assigned by random table) then received Yobine 0.05 mg/lb IV or placebo; each dog also served as its own pre/post-injection control. 258 cases enrolled, 71 unusable
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Sedation times (recumbency, arousal, walk), analgesia (prick response), clinical signs, heart rate and respiration rate, observed for at least 35 minutes
effectiveness.result: Yobine significantly shortened arousal time (least-squares means: 12.25 vs 21.55 min after IV xylazine, 17.59 vs 21.75 after IM, 14.81 vs 26.27 after SC) and walk time (14.55 vs 32.25, 19.39 vs 44.85, 17.19 vs 35.52 min), increased heart and respiratory rates, and decreased analgesia (prick test) versus placebo in xylazine-treated dogs; no adverse effects reported
effectiveness.quote: Therefore, 187 cases were used in the trials.

adverse_reactions.term: No adverse effects reported (pivotal field study, Yobine vs placebo after xylazine)
Increased CNS activity (brief seizures and muscle 'tumors' [sic]) in dose-titration group four (1x xylazine 0.5 mg/lb followed by 5x yohimbine 0.25 mg/lb IV)
adverse_reactions.quote: No adverse effects were reported, except increase CNS activity (brief seizures 6. and muscle tumors) in two dogs in group four.

notes: Original NADA. General Information gives no recommended dosage, so dose_regimen is the pivotal field-study dose (0.05 mg/lb IV). Field-study Table I (least-squares means) was flattened by PDF extraction; column order is IV-xylazine/Yohimbine, IV/Placebo, IM/Yohimbine, IM/Placebo, SC/Yohimbine, SC/Placebo: 'Arousal time 12.25 21.55 17.59 21.75 14.81 26.27'; 'Walk time 14.55 32.25 19.39 44.85 17.19 35.52'; 'Difference in heart rate prior to and post injection 15.90 61.45 13.17 58.83 18.28 60.03'. Study conclusion verbatim (PDF typo): 'Yobin e significantly shortened the arousal time, increased the heart and respiratory rates, and decreased analgesia in xylazine-treated dogs.' A separate dose-titration study (15 female and 15 male dogs in five groups; xylazine 1x 0.5 mg/lb or 5x 2.5 mg/lb IV followed 5 minutes later by yohimbine 0x, 0.2x 0.01 mg/lb, 1x 0.05 mg/lb or 5x 0.25 mg/lb IV) concluded Yobine was safe at 0.01 to 0.25 mg/lb and effective at 0.05 to 0.25 mg/lb; its only adverse event (group four) is recorded under adverse_reactions. target_animal_safety is the acute toxicity study (0X/1X/3X/5X, 6 dogs per group, 3 doses at 6 hr intervals). Several quotes contain interleaved outline numerals ('6.') from PDF extraction. No PK data in the summary.

indication.text: Chemical sterilization in 3 to 10 month old male dogs
indication.quote: Neutersol ® Injectable Solution is indicated for chemical sterilization in 3 to 10 month old male dogs.

dose_regimen.dose: 0.2 to 1.0 mL per testicle (2.6 to 13.1 mg zinc) by testicular width: 10-12 mm 0.2 mL; 13-15 mm 0.3 mL; 16-18 mm 0.5 mL; 19-21 mm 0.7 mL; 22-24 mm 0.8 mL; 25-27 mm 1.0 mL
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Dose per testicle chosen from testicular width measured at its widest point with a metric (mm) caliper; each mL contains 13.1 mg zinc as zinc gluconate
dose_regimen.quote: One injection is administered per testicle. Dose per testicle is based on testicular width as determined by measuring each testicle at its widest point using a metric scale (mm) caliper. The dose table is illustrated in Table 1. TABLE 1 DOSE CORRESPONDING TO TESTICULAR WIDTH Dose Per Testicle Range of Testicular Width (mm) mL (mg Zinc) 10-12 0.2 2.6 13-15 0.3 3.9 16-18 0.5 6.6 19-21 0.7 9.2 22-24 0.8 10.5 25-27 1.0 13.1

target_animal_safety.duration: Injections on Days 0 and 14 (planned third injection on Day 28 not administered because testicles were too hard and small to inject); 2 month study with necropsy at Week 8
target_animal_safety.n_animals: 24 male Beagle dogs, 6 months of age (four groups incl. placebo control)

findings.finding: Third injection (Day 28) could not be given because treated testicles were too hard to penetrate and had decreased in size
findings.quote: The third injection was attem pted on Day 28 but was not administered because the testicles were too hard for the needle to penetrate and the decreased testicular size made injection difficult.

findings.finding: No effect on body weight, body temperature, complete blood counts, serum chemistries or gross pathology
findings.quote: Zinc gluconate neutralized by arginine had no effect on bod y weight, body temperature, complete blood counts, serum chemistries, and gross pathology.

findings.finding: Transient testicular swelling in all treated dogs, peaking 24-48 hours after the first injection and 24 hours after the second
findings.quote: All treated dogs displayed transient testicular swelling. The peak swelling occurred between 24-48 hours after the first injection and 24 hours after the second injection.

findings.finding: Dose-related seminiferous tubule atrophy (1.25% control, 65.6% 1X, 74.2% 1.5X, 80.3% 2X); testicular and epididymal weights decreased in all treated groups
findings.quote: Seminiferous tubules of the treated groups displayed a greater percentage of atrophy compared to the control group (1.25% in the control group, 65.6% in the 1X group, 74.2% in the 1.5X group and 80.3% in the 2X group).

findings.finding: Serious scrotal lesions (purulent discharge, necrosis) in 4 dogs, one requiring surgical castration; associated with movement during injection, pre-existing skin lesion, or injecting against resistance
findings.quote: More serious scrotal lesions (purulent discharge and necrosis) were seen in 4 dogs, including 1 dog that required surgical castration due to necrosis of approximately one-half of the scrotal length.

findings.finding: Adverse reactions at 1X, 1.5X and 2X: transient discomfort when sitting (all groups), swelling 24-48 h after injections (all groups), difficulty walking at 24 h after first injection (2X), scrotal pain 24 h after second injection (2X)
findings.quote: Zinc gluconate neutralized by arginine injected at 1X, 1.5X, and 2X the recommended dose (volume) caused the following adverse reactions: transient discomfort 14 when sitting down (all groups), swelling at 24-48 hours after the first and second injections (all groups), difficulty walking 24 hours after the first injection (2X), and scrotal pain at 24 hours after the second injection (2X).

findings.finding: Average serum testosterone lower than control in all treated groups at week 8
findings.quote: The average testosterone levels for all groups treated with zinc gluconate neutralized by arginine were less than that of the control group at week 8.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Purpose: To determine the effect of zinc gluconate neutralized by arginine administered at 1X, 1.5X and 2X the recommended dose for three times the duration of treatment. e. Animals: 24 male Beagle dogs, 6 months of age, average testicular width of 15.2 mm, 16-21 lbs body weight.

effectiveness.design: Multi-site (Arizona, Florida, Missouri, New York) clinical field study with historical control (semen analyses of normal intact male dogs). 270 male dogs of various breeds, 2.5-10 months old, testicular width 10-27 mm, received a single intratesticular injection per testicle dosed by width (0.2-1.0 mL); 225 completed; dogs followed at least 6 months
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Treatment success at Month 6: aspermia, azoospermia, necrospermia or oligospermia (<20 million sperm/mL); failure: 80% progressive forward motility and >20 million sperm/mL
effectiveness.result: Effectiveness 99.6%: of 224 dogs, one treatment failure; 171 aspermic (76.3%), 50 azoospermic (22.3%), 1 necrospermic (0.5%), 1 oligospermic (0.5%)
effectiveness.quote: Semen was collected from 224 dogs at Month 6. Based on the criteria above, the effectiveness was 99.6%. Of the 224 dogs, there was one treatment failure, 171 dogs were aspermic (76.3%), 50 were azoospermic (22.3%), 1 was necrospermic (0.5%), and 1 was oligospermic (0.5%).

notes: Original NADA 141-217 for Neutersol® (later marketed as Zeuterin™, the catalogue name). The parser did not split sections (whole body captured as 'effectiveness'), so fields were taken from the raw text. Adverse-reaction rows are field-study Table 6 (Adverse Reaction / Number of Animals (n = 270) / Percentage); denominators are the 270 injected dogs and there was no concurrent control group (historical control), so 'control' is null. Table 6 rows not captured: Kicking 1 (0.3%), Scrotal Irritation 3 (1.1%), Biting and Licking 2 (0.7%), Scrotal Swelling 2 (0.7%), Scrotal Irritation & Dermatitis 2 (0.7%), Scrotal Ulceration 1, Scrotal Infection 1, Dry Scrotal Skin 1, Scrotal Bruising 1, Preputial Swelling 1, Scrotal Sore 1 (each 0.3%), Diarrhea 5 (1.9%), Leukocytosis 2 (0.7%). Of 270 dogs injected, 225 completed (28 not returned by owners, 10 castrated, 5 died, 2 euthanized); 224 had a Month 6 semen analysis; two Month-6 successes showed increased sperm counts at Month 12. Target animal safety was a GLP study at 1X/1.5X/2X by volume (6 dogs per group, placebo = bacteriostatic water) with injections on Days 0 and 14 (Day 28 injection not feasible); doses reflected an earlier version of the dose table. Also reported but not captured as separate records: a 16-month pilot (27 Beagles, 0.2 and 0.5 mL) and a 2-year dose determination study (40 Beagles, 0.25/0.30/0.35 mL; 0.3 mL chosen for 13 mm testicle). Several quotes preserve PDF-extraction artifacts ('attem pted', 'bod y', 'Neutersol ®', embedded page number '14'). No PK data.
